newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - DASA wants Siemens defence business.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - DASA wants Siemens defence business.

text.p: Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) said on Monday it wanted to buy Siemens AG's defence electronics operations in a tender expected to start soon.
Board member Werner Heinzmann said that DASA had a clear interest in taking over Siemens's missiles business. "There is an excellent fit," he told a news conference.
Heinzmann said that DASA, a unit of car maker Daimler-Benz AG, would join the bidding for the Siemens defence electronics unit in the competitive tender expected to go ahead soon.
DASA was also interested in merging the missiles business of Nuremberg-based Diehl GmbH & Co with its own operations as part of an overall restructuring, he added.
Due to defence budget cuts DASA wants to cut its own missiles workforce to 1,050 from 1,500 due and is considering closing its plant at Nabern in the southwestern state of Baden-Wuerttemberg.
Little progress had been made in the talks so far, however, because privately-owned Diehl had not been prepared to give up majority control even though its missiles business was smaller than DASA's.

Heinzmann said a tender for the Siemens defence electronics operations -- part of a business area which posted sales of 1.6 billion marks ($925 million) last year -- should begin in the next few weeks, and there were likely to be both German and foreign bidders.

He called on German politicians to make clear their interest in keeping the Siemens unit in German hands for both security and industrial reasons. "I expect the political side to get involved and express its opinions," Heinzmann said.
If the Siemens defence electronics business went abroad, that would significantly worsen Germany's position in the current wave of European defence industry mergers, he said.
The outlook for cross-border defence cooperation has changed since DASA put talks on joint missiles projects with France's Aerospatiale on ice recently.

Matra and Alcatel are seeking to buy French defence and electronics business Thomson. DASA has held talks on cooperation with both interested parties, and the outcome of the Thomson sale will have a significant bearing on future prospects, Heinzmann said.
DASA's defence and civil systems business employed 9,000 workers last year and turned over 2.6 billion marks. Heinzmann said that this figure would rise this year to 2.8 billion marks.

Heinzmann also said that the division's Dornier unit would return to profit this year following the sale of its regional passenger jet business to U.S. Fairchild Corp. Last year Dornier made a loss of 423 million marks.
